info.title: Agent Orchestrator
info.description:
Yuno AI Agent Orchestration Platform — backend API.

Stack: FastAPI · LangGraph · PostgreSQL · Redis · Arq.

**Auth.** All non-public endpoints require an `Authorization: Bearer <access_token>`
header. Obtain tokens via `POST /api/v1/auth/login` and rotate via
`POST /api/v1/auth/refresh`. The access token is valid for 12 hours; the
refresh token for 30 days.

**Error envelope.** Every non-2xx response is `{"error": {"code", "message", "details"}}`.
Switch on `code` in the frontend (it's stable); render `message` to the user;
inspect `details` for structured per-error data.

post.description: Creates a new user and returns access + refresh tokens (auto-login). Email must be unique; password must be at least 8 characters.

Exchanges email + password for an access token (12h) and a refresh token (30d). Send the access token as `Authorization: Bearer <token>` on every protected request. Rotate via `POST /auth/refresh` before the access token expires.

post.summary: Exchange a refresh token for a new pair
post.description: Returns a freshly issued access + refresh token pair. The presented refresh token is revoked atomically — clients must store the new one and discard the old.

Revokes the presented refresh token immediately. The corresponding access token expires naturally (no server-side revocation list for access tokens — keep TTL short). Idempotent: revoking an already-invalid token returns 204.

get.description: Returns the user identified by the bearer access token.
Returns every workspace the authenticated user is a member of, with the user's role in each. Powers the landing-page workspace picker.

post.description: Creates a workspace owned by the authenticated user. The caller is automatically added as a `workspace_members` row with role `owner`. Workspace `id` and `slug` are generated server-side.

delete.description: Marks the workspace as deleted (sets `deleted_at = now()`). The workspace immediately disappears from `GET /workspaces` and nested endpoints (workflows, agents, …) return 403 for it. **Only the workspace `owner` can delete.** Data is preserved on disk; recovery would be a future admin tool.

get.description: Returns every workflow in the given workspace, newest first. The caller must be a member of the workspace (any role).

post.summary: Create a workflow in a workspace
post.description:
Creates a workflow. The `graph` field is optional — when omitted, the canvas is seeded with a single `start` node so the builder has an anchor to wire from.

Agent ids referenced by `agent` nodes (if any) must already exist in this workspace. Structural checks (start/end presence, no orphans) are **not** enforced here — only on transition to `published` via PATCH.

get.summary: Get a workflow with its full graph
get.description: Returns the workflow including `graph` (React Flow shape) and `compiled_graph` (langgraph-ready normalized shape). The builder uses `graph`; the runtime dispatcher reads `compiled_graph`.

patch.description:
Partial update of metadata: `name`, `description`, `status`, `settings`. The graph itself is updated via `PATCH /workspaces/{ws}/workflows/{id}/graph` so autosave from the canvas can stay cheap.

Setting `status` to `published` runs strict structural checks on the current graph and 422s with `issues` if anything is wrong.

delete.description: Marks the workflow as deleted. Idempotent — already-deleted workflows return 404.

patch.description: Dedicated PATCH for the React Flow canvas autosave. Replaces `graph_json` wholesale and re-derives `compiled_graph` (langgraph-ready normalization with `add_conditional_edges` grouping). Agent refs are validated against this workspace; in-progress graphs (missing end node, agent nodes without an `agentId`) are tolerated.

get.description: Returns metadata for every webhook on this workflow. The plaintext token is **never** returned — only the prefix used for UI hinting. Use this endpoint to display the integration list and rotate keys.

schema.title: Response Webhooks Get List For Workflow

post.description: Generates a fresh signing token for this workflow and returns the plaintext value **exactly once**. Subsequent reads only see the prefix. Treat the response like an API key — copy it into your integration immediately. If you lose it, mint a new one and revoke the old.

delete.description: Marks the token revoked. Subsequent calls to the ingress URL with this token return 404. Revocation is idempotent — calling on an already-revoked webhook is a no-op.

get.description: Returns every agent in the workspace, newest first. Light shape: id, name, description, created_at, created_by. Use `GET /workspaces/{ws_id}/agents/{agent_id}` for the full config.

post.summary: Create an agent in a workspace
post.description:
Creates an agent (workflow node). The five mandatory fields are the minimum LangGraph needs to materialize the node at runtime via `create_react_agent(model, tools, prompt=...)`:

- `name` — display name
- `role` — short role label (used in conversation routing)
- `system_prompt` — the LLM's system message
- `model_provider` — LLM provider key (must be a configured one)
- `model_name` — provider-specific model id

All other fields (description, sampling params, memory/guardrails/limits/interaction-rules/skills configs) default to sensible values and can be edited later via the agent editor.

get.description: Returns every field needed to render the agent editor: prompt, model + sampling params, memory/schedule/guardrails/limits/skills configs (opaque JSONB), and audit fields.

patch.description:
Partial update — every field is optional. Omit a field to leave it unchanged. Pass `provider_credentials: {"api_key": "..."}` to rotate the BYOK key; pass `{}` to clear it (the agent will fall back to the user vault / server-level key at run time).

Changing `model_provider` validates the new provider against the supported list. Key resolution is **not** re-checked here — the agent can sit in `draft` with no key until you actually run it.

get.description:
Returns everything the agent-builder UI needs to render the create-agent form without hard-coding anything:

- `providers` — every LLM provider the server knows about, with a curated recommended-model list, the **per-user** `is_configured` flag (true iff either the server has a global key for it OR this user has saved one in their LLM credentials vault), and per-agent config fields with bounds.
- `fields.mandatory` / `fields.optional` — every `CreateAgentRequest` field split by required-ness, with type/length/range constraints.
- `tools` — built-in tools available to attach to agents (empty in v1 until the tool registry is wired).
- `tool_entry_shape` — the expected shape of each item when attaching tools to an agent's `skills_config.tools` array.
- `provider_credentials_shape` — schema for the optional per-agent BYOK field on agent creation.

get.summary: List my LLM provider credential statuses
get.description: Returns one entry per supported provider (`openai`, `gemini`, `groq`), indicating whether the current user has saved credentials. The actual API keys are never returned.

get.summary: Get credential status for one provider
get.description: Returns the configured-status + non-secret metadata for one provider. If unconfigured, `is_configured` is `false` and other fields are null.

post.description: Upsert credentials for one LLM provider. Returns 204 with no body — the frontend's `llmProviderApi.registerCredential` parses with `z.void()`. Refetch via `GET /llm-providers/{provider}/credentials` if you need the updated status. The submitted payload fully replaces existing credentials (no deep merge); the actual key is stored in Postgres JSONB, never echoed back, and redacted in HTTP access logs.

delete.description: Deletes the user's stored credentials for one provider. Idempotent — deleting non-existent credentials returns 204.

get.summary: List all registered built-in tool handlers
get.description: Built-ins are the handlers compiled into the platform (calculator, web_search, ask_agent, …). Use this endpoint to populate the tool-creation UI's `handler` picker for `type=builtin` tools.
Workspace-scoped tools plus global built-ins, newest first. Filter with `type=`, `category=`, `status=`.

post.summary: Create a tool in a workspace
post.description: Creates a workspace-scoped tool. Required: `name`, `description`, `type`. Most useful for `type=http` (REST integrations) and `type=builtin` (register a registered handler). Returns the full ToolDetail; a `v1` snapshot is created on the side and visible via `GET .../versions`.

patch.description: Partial update. Pass `publish_new_version: true` to snapshot the result so workflow runs pinned to the older version keep using its schema and config.

get.summary: List published versions of a tool

post.summary: Run a tool with synthetic input (test console)
post.description: Dispatches the tool synchronously and returns a fully-resolved `ToolExecutionDetail` (status, output, logs, duration). Pass `dry_run: true` to render the resolved request payload without actually calling the backend — useful for inspecting templating.

get.summary: Get a single tool execution + its log stream
List tool executions waiting on human approval

post.summary: Approve or reject a pending tool execution

get.summary: List tools attached to an agent

post.summary: Attach a tool to an agent
post.description: Grants the agent the right to call `tool_id` during a run. Use the `permission` object to require human approval, cap calls per run, or stamp default input values.

delete.summary: Detach a tool from an agent

get.summary: List workflow runs in a workspace
get.description: Paginated list of runs, newest first. Optionally filter by `workflow_id` and/or `status`. Returns the light shape — use `GET /workspaces/{ws}/runs/{run_id}` for per-step IO and the event stream.

get.summary: Get a run with per-step IO and the event stream
get.description: Returns the run row plus every `workflow_run_nodes` entry (per-step input/output/timing/error) and the first 500 `runtime_events` rows (timeline view). Use this on the run detail page.

delete.summary: Delete a run and its history
delete.description: Hard delete — removes the run row plus all `workflow_run_nodes` and `runtime_events` (cascading FK). If the run is still queued/running, it is cancelled first so no worker writes back to a vanishing row.

post.summary: Cancel a queued or running workflow run
post.description: Marks the run `cancelled` and asks arq to abort the job. Queued jobs are removed from the queue before any work starts; running jobs receive a cancel signal — the executor's `finally` block is responsible for flushing state. Returns 422 if the run is already in a terminal state (`completed` / `failed` / `cancelled`).

Public ingress endpoint for external integrations. POST a JSON object — it becomes the run's initial state. The endpoint returns **202 Accepted** with the new run id; execution happens asynchronously on the worker.

No bearer auth: the token in the URL is the only auth factor. Treat it as a secret.

Returns 404 (not 401/403) for any auth failure to avoid leaking which workflows exist.

404.description: Webhook not found, revoked, or token mismatch

422.description: Body is not a JSON object

get.description: Returns 200 if the API process is up. No auth required.

AgentCapabilities.description: Everything needed to render the agent-creation form.

provider_credentials_configured.title: Provider Credentials Configured
provider_credentials_configured.description: True iff the agent carries its own provider credentials. The actual key is never returned by any endpoint.

AgentDetail.title: AgentDetail
AgentDetail.description:
Full agent configuration. Returned by the detail endpoint.

The JSONB blobs (memory/schedule/guardrails/interaction_rules/limits/
skills) are returned as opaque dicts here — frontend renders them via
the agent-editor module. Backend doesn't impose a schema on these
fields yet; that comes when we wire the runtime executor.

created_by.title: Created By
created_by.description: User who authored the agent. Null if that user was deleted.

AgentSummary.title: AgentSummary
AgentSummary.description: Light shape for the list endpoint — no JSONB configs (kilobytes+ per row).

name.description: Human-readable display name shown in the workflow builder.

system_prompt.title: System Prompt
system_prompt.description: System prompt the LLM receives. Becomes `prompt=` in `create_react_agent`.

model_provider.title: Model Provider
model_provider.description: LLM provider key. Must match a configured provider (`openai`, `gemini`, `groq`).

description.title: Description
description.description: Free-text description shown in the agent picker / hover card.

provider_credentials.description: Per-agent LLM provider credentials. When omitted, the agent uses the server-level API key for `model_provider` from `.env`. **Required** when the provider is not globally configured.

examples.description: Classifies inbound tickets and dispatches to specialists.
examples.name: Support Router
examples.system_prompt: You are the front-line router for inbound customer messages. Classify each message into one of: billing, technical, sales. Hand off to the appropriate specialist agent.

description.title: Description
description.description: Free-text, but treat this as the LLM-facing tool docstring — the model uses it to decide when to call the tool. Be specific.

input_schema.title: Input Schema
input_schema.description: Draft-07 JSON Schema describing the input arguments.

output_schema.title: Output Schema
output_schema.description: Draft-07 JSON Schema describing the tool's return shape.

config.title: Config
config.description: Per-type executor config. Shape matches one of `HttpToolConfig`, `MessagingToolConfig`, `AgentHandoffToolConfig`, `WebhookToolConfig`, `BuiltinToolConfig` depending on `type`.

examples.description: Send a message to a Slack channel. Use whenever a human needs to be notified or a result needs to be shared.
examples.name: Send Slack message

name.title: Name
name.description: Display name for the webhook — used to identify it in the UI when rotating keys.

token_prefix.title: Token Prefix
token_prefix.description: First 8 chars of the plaintext token. Safe to show in UI for disambiguation.

token.title: Token
token.description: Full plaintext token. Shown once at creation.

url.title: Url
url.description: Full webhook URL ready to paste into an integration.

CreateWebhookResponse.title: CreateWebhookResponse
CreateWebhookResponse.description:
One-shot create response — includes the plaintext token + URL.

The plaintext token is **never returned again**. Surface it to the user
immediately and treat it like an API key on the client side.

graph.description: Optional initial graph; defaults to an empty canvas with a single `start` node.

name.title: Name
name.description: Human-readable workspace name. Slug is derived server-side.

code.title: Code
code.description: Stable upper-snake error code. Switch on this in the UI.

message.title: Message
message.description: Human-readable summary; safe to surface to the user.

details.title: Details
details.description: Structured per-error data (validation errors, conflict keys, etc).

ErrorDetail.title: ErrorDetail
ErrorDetail.description:
The `error` field of every non-2xx response.

Mirrors what ``app.core.errors.register_exception_handlers`` emits, so
the OpenAPI schema matches the real wire format byte-for-byte.

ErrorEnvelope.title: ErrorEnvelope
ErrorEnvelope.description: Top-level error response shape returned by every error path.

agent_id.title: Agent Id
agent_id.description: Run the tool as if invoked from this agent (uses its permissions/guardrails).

dry_run.title: Dry Run
dry_run.description: When true, render the resolved request payload without dispatching it.

ExecuteToolRequest.title: ExecuteToolRequest
ExecuteToolRequest.description: Synchronous test invocation from the tool console.

FieldSpec.title: FieldSpec
FieldSpec.description: One CreateAgentRequest field, in a UI-friendly form.

updated_at.title: Updated At
updated_at.description: When the credential was last set/updated. Null if unconfigured.

LLMCredentialStatus.title: LLMCredentialStatus
LLMCredentialStatus.description:
Status of one provider's credential for the current user.

Never echoes the `api_key`. Surfaces only the public fields the FE
needs to render the settings card: provider, configured flag, the
non-secret bits (base_url, organization), and timestamps.

LLMCredentialsListResponse.title: LLMCredentialsListResponse
LLMCredentialsListResponse.description: List of credential statuses, one entry per supported provider.

refresh_token.title: Refresh Token
refresh_token.description: Refresh token to revoke. The matching access token expires naturally.

name.title: Name
name.description: Provider-specific model id sent to the API.

key.title: Key
key.description: Use this as `model_provider` when creating an agent.

is_configured.title: Is Configured
is_configured.description: True iff the server has an API key for this provider. Agents using a non-configured provider cannot be executed.

default_model.title: Default Model
default_model.description: The model_name we recommend by default. Null if no models are catalogued.

config_fields.title: Config Fields
config_fields.description: Per-agent LLM config knobs (temperature, max_tokens, top_p) with bounds.

ProviderConfigField.title: ProviderConfigField
ProviderConfigField.description: A single tunable field on an agent's LLM config.

base_url.title: Base Url
base_url.description: Custom API base URL. Useful for proxies (OpenAI-compatible endpoints, Groq mirrors).

ProviderCredentialsConfig.title: ProviderCredentialsConfig
ProviderCredentialsConfig.description:
Per-agent override of the server-level LLM provider credentials.

Optional. When set, ``api_key`` overrides ``settings.<provider>_api_key``
for this agent's runs. ``base_url`` + ``organization`` are honored where
the provider's SDK supports them (OpenAI; Groq supports `base_url`).

Security:
- The api_key is **stored as-is in JSONB** (Postgres TDE only). Treat
  Postgres read access as equivalent to having the key.
- The api_key is **never returned in any GET response** — only a
  ``provider_credentials_configured: bool`` flag.
- Whole ``provider_credentials`` subtree is redacted in HTTP access logs.

when_required.title: When Required
when_required.default: When the chosen `model_provider` has `is_configured: false`, the agent must include `provider_credentials.api_key`. Otherwise it's optional and overrides the server-level key for this agent's runs only.

storage_note.title: Storage Note
storage_note.default: Stored as JSONB in Postgres. Never returned in GET responses — only a `provider_credentials_configured: bool` flag is exposed. Redacted in HTTP access logs.

ProviderCredentialsShape.title: ProviderCredentialsShape
ProviderCredentialsShape.description:
Schema reference for the agent's per-agent `provider_credentials` form field.

BYOK (bring-your-own-key) lets each agent carry its own provider creds
that override the server-level key at run time. **Required** when the
chosen `model_provider` shows `is_configured: false` (server has no
global key for it).

refresh_token.title: Refresh Token
refresh_token.description: Opaque refresh token issued by /login or a previous /refresh.

RunAcknowledgement.title: RunAcknowledgement
RunAcknowledgement.description:
Returned by the public webhook ingress.

202 Accepted — the run is queued, not executed.

RunDetail.title: RunDetail
RunDetail.description:
Full run with per-step rows and the event stream.

`nodes` is the canonical "what happened at each step" view (in/out
payloads, status, timing). `events` is the granular append-only log —
same data sliced finer (started/completed/tool.called/branch.matched)
for live UIs and audit trails.

base_url.title: Base Url
base_url.description: Custom API base URL. Useful for OpenAI-compatible endpoints / Groq mirrors.

SetLLMCredentialsRequest.title: SetLLMCredentialsRequest
SetLLMCredentialsRequest.description:
Set or update credentials for a single LLM provider.

Upsert semantics: if the user already has a row for this provider,
the existing row's `credentials` JSONB is overwritten with the new
payload (use full replacement, not deep-merge — clearer behavior).

access_token.title: Access Token
access_token.description: JWT access token. Send as `Authorization: Bearer <token>`.

refresh_token.title: Refresh Token
refresh_token.description: Opaque refresh token. Store securely; do not log.

ToolCapability.title: ToolCapability
ToolCapability.description:
One built-in tool offered to agents.

`parameters_schema` is JSON Schema for the tool's input — the LLM
sees this when deciding whether to call the tool.

ToolDetail.title: ToolDetail
ToolDetail.description: Full tool definition. Returned by the detail endpoint and after writes.

ToolEntryShape.title: ToolEntryShape
ToolEntryShape.description:
The shape of each entry inside ``agent.skills_config["tools"]``.

When attaching a tool to an agent, append one of these objects to
the tools array. ``name`` must match a tool from ``tools[].name``.
``options`` is freeform — tool-specific overrides (rate limits, API
creds, prompt fragments) interpreted by the tool's executor.

ToolSummary.title: ToolSummary
ToolSummary.description: Light shape for the list endpoint.

UpdateAgentRequest.title: UpdateAgentRequest
UpdateAgentRequest.description:
Patch shape for the agent editor.

Every field is optional. `provider_credentials` lets the user rotate
the BYOK key in place — pass `{"api_key": "..."}` to overwrite the
stored credential block. Pass an explicit empty object `{}` to clear
BYOK and fall back to the user vault / global key.

publish_new_version.title: Publish New Version
publish_new_version.description: If true, snapshot the updated tool to a new `tool_versions` row before saving. Workflow runs pinned to older versions keep executing the original behaviour.

UpdateToolRequest.title: UpdateToolRequest
UpdateToolRequest.description: Partial update — every field optional. Omit to leave unchanged.

UpdateWorkflowGraphRequest.title: UpdateWorkflowGraphRequest
UpdateWorkflowGraphRequest.description:
Dedicated PATCH body for autosave from the canvas.

The editor debounces every node/edge change and ships this payload —
keeping it separate from `UpdateWorkflowRequest` means the autosave
path is cheap to validate and never accidentally mutates name/status.

UpdateWorkflowRequest.title: UpdateWorkflowRequest
UpdateWorkflowRequest.description: Partial update for non-graph workflow metadata.

token_prefix.title: Token Prefix
token_prefix.description: First 8 chars of the plaintext token. Safe to show in UI for disambiguation.

WebhookSummary.title: WebhookSummary
WebhookSummary.description: List/read shape — never includes the plaintext token.

WorkflowDetail.title: WorkflowDetail
WorkflowDetail.description: Full workflow — includes graph_json + compiled_graph + settings.

WorkflowEdgeCondition.title: WorkflowEdgeCondition
WorkflowEdgeCondition.description:
Routing predicate on a graph edge.

`always`  — unconditional (default when omitted)
`equals`  — `state[path] == value`
`expr`    — safe DSL expression (parsed at compile time, not eval'd here)

viewport.title: Viewport
viewport.description: Optional React Flow viewport (`{x, y, zoom}`).

WorkflowGraph.title: WorkflowGraph
WorkflowGraph.description: Raw React Flow graph as stored in `workflows.graph_json`.

data.title: Data
data.description: Opaque per-node payload. The builder writes `label` + `config`; the compiler reads `config.agentId` / `config.toolId` / `config.expression` depending on the node type.

created_by.title: Created By
created_by.description: User who authored the workflow. Null if that user was deleted.

WorkflowSummary.title: WorkflowSummary
WorkflowSummary.description: Light shape for list endpoints — no graph_json (kilobytes+ per row).

examples.description: Routes inbound questions to the right specialist agent.
examples.name: Support triage

role.title: Role
role.description: Current user's role in this workspace.

WorkspaceSummary.title: WorkspaceSummary
WorkspaceSummary.description:
Shape returned by the landing-page list endpoint.

Includes the role the *current* user has in the workspace so the UI
can render the "owner" / "viewer" badge without a second call.

BearerAuth.description: Paste your access token (without the `Bearer ` prefix).
